verdicts.item: qwq:32b Mac result and Ollama facts
verdicts.evidence: qwq.md: 69/189/208/75/70/61 s, median 76 s, slowest 6:00, 'Nothing' needed, no turn exceeded 90 s, roughly a dozen turns in 208 s, 150 s named as first fix, 'six other models on this list carry one'. Manifest: 19,851,336,480 bytes sha256:7ccc6415b2c7; params blob {repeat_penalty 1, temperature 0.6, top_k 40, top_p 0.95}. Tags page 009cb3f08d74 20GB 40K. ollama.com/library/qwq shows one capability span 'tools' (line 401); the two 'thinking' hits are description text, not a badge.

KV per token: 7b 28x4x128x2x2 = 56 KiB (64k = 3.5 GiB); 14b 48x8x128x4 = 192 KiB (32k f16 6 GiB, 64k q8_0 about 6.4 GiB, total 14.8 GiB plus compute = 15.3-15.8 GiB, at the limit); 32b 64x8x128x4 = 256 KiB (64k f16 16 GiB). 18.49 GiB weights cannot fit in 15.47 GiB. Per-layer split about 0.29 GiB weights + 0.25 GiB (f16) or 0.13 GiB (q8_0) KV gives about 26-34 layers resident, matching the record. Layer split ignores the separate output/embedding tensors (about 0.6+ GiB), which slightly lowers the resident count, within the record's ranges.

verdicts.item: Speed reasoning (bandwidth scaling and DDR5 spill)
verdicts.evidence: 614 GB/s verified on apple.com. 7b: 4.68 GB -> 896/4.68 = 191, 614/4.68 = 131, matches '190 vs 130'. 32B spill: about 9.9 GB from DDR5 at 60-80 GB/s gives about 6-8 tok/s, consistent with 5-8. qwq 208 s / ~12 turns = ~17 s per turn, as stated.
verdicts.correction: For qwen2.5:14b the record's '107 vs 73 tok/s theoretical' divides GB/s by GiB (8.37). With bytes (8.99 GB) the ceilings are about 100 vs 68 tok/s; the 1.46x ratio and the 85-90 tok/s expectation are unaffected.

verdicts.item: Recommendations (7b try-here-first, 14b and coder worth-trying, 32b and qwq skip-here)
verdicts.evidence: Follow from the verified sizes, fit arithmetic and Mac results; no contrary evidence found.

summary: I found nothing that refutes the qwen-older record. The Mac results for all five tags match the libredb pages (qwen/qwen2.5.md, qwen/qwen2.5-coder.md, qwen/qwq.md) cell for cell. The Ollama facts also match: layer byte sizes, tag ids, 32K/40K context, the qwq params blob and the 'tools'-only badge on qwq, checked against the live registry manifests and the ollama.com tag pages. apple.com confirms that a 64 GB M5 Max is the 40-core part at 614 GB/s. The fit arithmetic checks out, and so does the KB status mapping: none of the five appears in model-selection.md, only in the community-benchmarks rows :75-77 and :301. One small correction: the 14b decode ceilings divide GB/s by GiB. Computed in bytes they are about 100 vs 68 tok/s, not 107 vs 73. The ratio and the 85-90 tok/s laptop estimate do not change. One nuance on qwen2.5:14b: 'pure defaults' still includes the one plan ask that the default offers a model with no entry (model-tuning.md:152-153).
